localChanges: A game that was loaded from a save and then saved again now carries on with the same random events as a game that was never interrupted (closes #17).

log: `restore(seed, calls)` moved the generator onto `seed`'s stream but left `seed()` returning the seed it was constructed with. The default instance is constructed from `Date.now()`, so any process that took control with `restore` and then saved recorded a clock value as the seed: loading that file resumed a different stream at the right draw count.

This made the played-on hash of web-renderer's load suite vary between runs (six values over 30 runs, one per advance a single random research pick could land on), and affects any game in the browser that is loaded and then saved again. With the fix the loaded game matches uninterrupted play on every run (civ-clone/web-renderer#17).

Adds the standard `build-on-push.yml` (Node 22, pnpm, no lock file), with the compile step that fails when the committed `.js` is stale, and makes `prettier:check` actually check (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).
Nothing installs from it: CI resolves with pnpm and no lock file, as a consumer does (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).

`restore` normalised the seed it reports (`>>> 0`) but computed the state from the raw value, so after restoring a negative or fractional seed the generator was not at the position `seed()` and `calls()` describe, and a generator restored from them drew differently. The state is now computed from the normalised seed, as `createRng` does.

`git diff --exit-code` only sees tracked files, so a new module whose `.js` was never added passed, and the published package would omit it. The check now fails on modified or untracked `.js`, `.d.ts` and `.js.map`, listing them, and ignores everything else, such as the lock file the install writes.

The standard workflow from civ-clone/web-renderer#66: Node 22, pnpm with no lock file and web-renderer's settings. prettier:check now has --check, so it fails on unformatted files instead of printing them.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

StrategyRegistry.attempt broke ties between equal priorities with an RNG draw inside the sort comparator. How many numbers that drew depended on the sort, and every draw moved the game's seeded sequence, so it could not be used without changing play. It also recomputed priorities on every comparison, and `a - b` is NaN when both are Infinity (no Priority rule applies).

Now each Strategy's priority is computed once, ties go to registration order, and nothing is random. The RNG constructor argument is still accepted, for core-game's `new StrategyRegistry(rng)`, but not used, so core-random is no longer a dependency.
Strategy.attempt may return a Promise<boolean>. StrategyRegistry.attempt resolves a Promise<boolean> and awaits each attempt before the next, stopping at the first true.
Strategy.handles(action), default true, is a cheap filter checked before any Priority rule is evaluated or attempt is called.
StrategyRegistry.attemptAll(action) runs every handling Strategy in the same order, whatever each returns, for per-turn hooks that several plugins contribute to.

Nothing in the game calls StrategyRegistry.attempt yet. Strategy.test.ts's duplicates of the registry tests are removed; it used `spy` without `use(spies)` and only passed because StrategyRegistry.test.ts, loaded in the same run, calls it.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

getByKey scanned every note, and register and replace call it too. It now reads an EntityRegistry.index keyed on the note's key, which is fixed for the note's lifetime (replace swaps notes rather than re-keying one). Requires core-registry 0.1.3, the first version with index().

A save restores notes the same way: core-save-game's hydrate fills each entity before registering it into game.strategyNotes, so register files it under its key. There is a test that restores a note that way.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

It accepts anything with an id(), but only called it on a DataObject and used toString() on everything else, which gave "[object Object]" for, say, a plain object with an id(). Every current caller passes DataObjects or strings, so no existing key changes.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

The README still described Routines. It now covers handles, async attempt, attempt and attemptAll, and the contract: strategies are game-wide and stateless, take the player from action.player(), keep memory in notes keyed by player and unit, and can be run directly for one unit or city, e.g. to automate a human player's unit.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.
CI installs with pnpm and no lock file, and nothing reads this one.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

The example used RuleRegistry, TraitRegistry, Leader, Trait and the registry instances without importing them. Every library identifier is imported now, and the plugin-specific placeholders (MyAction, MyTrait, doSomethingWith) are listed as such.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

It lists the strategies that handle an action, in the order attempt tries them. A caller that needs to know which strategy produced a result, such as StrategyAIClient.chooseFromList attributing a choice to the strategy that accepted it, iterates them itself.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

The tests load the committed .js, so CI could pass on source that no longer type-checks, or whose compiled output was never rebuilt. CI now compiles with tsc --build --force and runs prettier:format, then fails if either changed a tracked file. --force because a fresh checkout's timestamps can make tsc --build treat the committed output as up to date and skip the compile.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.
